title: Deterministic worst-case polylogarithmic dynamic 2-edge-connectivity
formal: Does there exist a deterministic data structure for a simple undirected graph on a fixed vertex set \([n]\), with polynomial initialization and polynomial space, that supports edge insertion, edge deletion and pairwise two-edge-connectivity queries in \(O(\log^c(2+n))\) worst-case time each, for one absolute constant c?
definitions:
Initially the graph is specified by explicit adjacency lists. An insertion adds a currently absent unordered edge between distinct vertices; a deletion removes an existing edge. Both types may occur in any order. A query on distinct u,v asks whether there exist two u-to-v paths with no common edge. They may share internal vertices. Equivalently, u and v must remain connected after deleting any single edge of the current graph. Define a query with u=v to return true by convention.

A bridge is an edge whose deletion increases the number of connected components. The selected interface answers only the pair predicate; it need not list all bridges or report the two witnessing paths. It is not two-vertex-connectivity, which would require resistance to deleting an internal vertex.

The machine is a uniform word RAM with \(\Theta(\log n)\)-bit words, enough to address polynomial storage. Basic word arithmetic, bit operations, comparisons and a read or write cost one operation. Input size, identifiers and update arguments are explicit. For some fixed exponent d, initialization and storage are bounded by \(n^d\). The structure must answer exactly on every legal history and cannot use randomness. Each update and query has its own polylogarithmic bound; a small average over a long history does not qualify. Since execution is deterministic, histories may depend arbitrarily on previous answers.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction meeting the exact pair-query and worst-case bounds, or a complete Lean-checked impossibility theorem for this model. Amortized updates, randomized correctness, connectivity without resilience to an edge failure, or restrictions to planar embeddings do not settle the claim. A theorem reporting bridges can qualify only if it also yields the required pair-query interface and costs.
context:
Dynamic two-edge-connectivity is distinct from ordinary connectivity and from vertex biconnectivity. The recent general-graph work includes the pairwise edge-resilience problem in a fully dynamic framework.

The September 2026 preprint announces polylogarithmic worst-case algorithms that are randomized and work against adaptive adversaries. It explicitly identifies randomness in its static subroutine; it does not claim the unconditional deterministic algorithm requested here.
why: This asks whether resilience to one edge failure can be maintained without expensive occasional rebuilds.

import_provenance.original_statement: Maintain an undirected graph under edge insertions and deletions so that queries ask whether two vertices remain connected after any one edge failure. Can both updates and queries have deterministic polylogarithmic worst-case time?
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Deterministic polylogarithmic amortized bounds are known; requiring worst-case update bounds is essential. This is a strengthening of Italiano’s dynamic connectivity program.
